key_concepts: Weathering breaks down rocks into smaller particles.
Physical weathering and chemical weathering are two types of weathering.
Erosion transports Earth materials from one place to another.
Water, wind, and ice are agents of erosion.
Soil forms from weathered rocks and minerals.
Soil has distinct layers called horizons.
Leaching is the downward movement of particles in soil.
Soil is composed of minerals, air, water, and organic matter.
Organic matter comes from decomposed plant and animal remains.
Microorganisms help decompose organic matter in soil.
Soil is essential for sustaining life and plant growth.
